mainTopic: Doubtful ownership and disputed holdings: a ספק בכור grabbed by a כהן, the disputed bathhouse, two people holding a garment, קנין סודר, and a שטר held by a lender and a borrower
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof. A flock is exempt from מעשר בהמה because the פסוק demands a certain tenth, so the proof stands that a ספק בכור grabbed by a כהן is taken away from him. רב אחא מדפתי then asks which doubtful animals are subject to מעשר. The answer is the lambs used to redeem a ספק פטר חמור, following רב נחמן. The גמרא settles the disputed bathhouse with רב נחמן's rule that property you cannot win in court cannot be made הקדש. It squares that rule with רבי יוחנן by explaining that the bathhouse is land. Next, a ברייתא says that two people holding a garment each keep what is in their hands, and רב פפא explains that our משנה is about people holding only the fringes. From this רב משרשיא learns that grasping a 3x3 piece is enough for a קנין סודר, and רבא adds that gold on the garment is shared equally. Finally, a ברייתא about a lender and a borrower both holding a שטר leads to the debate over whether a note the borrower admits writing still needs confirming, and the amud ends by quoting the case of a note that fell into a judge's hands.

steps.title: The exemption comes from the verse: a certain tenth, not a doubtful one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that when a counted animal jumps back into the pen, the whole flock is exempt because the Torah requires a definite tenth. The same reasoning applies to the case under discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what must you say? The Torah said a certain tenth, and not an uncertain tenth. Here too: the Torah said a certain tenth, and not an uncertain tenth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an argument by pointing to the case of a counted animal that jumped back into the pen. That flock is exempt from מעשר בהמה only because the פסוק demands a definite tenth. The same is true here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone tried to explain the exemption from מעשר as a sign that the owner does not fully own the animals, as if a כהן who grabbed one could keep it. But the exemption comes from a separate rule in the פסוק (ויקרא 27:32): only an animal that is surely the tenth becomes מעשר. So that attempt fails, and the proof stands: a כהן who grabs a ספק בכור has it taken away from him.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain tenth: an animal that is definitely the tenth one counted
An uncertain tenth: an animal whose status as the tenth is in doubt
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Here too: applying the same reasoning to the current case

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the exemption here as a statement about ownership. The flock is exempt because of a technical rule in the פסוק (the tenth must be certain), not because the owner lacks full ownership.

phrases.english: Rather, what must you say?
The Torah said a certain tenth
and not an uncertain tenth.
Here too:
the Torah said a certain tenth
and not an uncertain tenth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the argument from the previous section, which compared this case to the counted animal that jumped back into the pen.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the exemption to a verse-based requirement (a definite tenth) rather than to the ownership status of the animals.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The exemption from מעשר might have seemed to tell us something about who owns the animals.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exemption comes from the פסוק's demand for a certain tenth. The same applies here.

steps.title: Which doubtful animals does the משנה mean? Not doubtful firstborns
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדפתי asks רבינא which ספיקות are meant. A ספק בכור cannot be the case, because מעשר applies only to an animal that is not already holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא מדפתי said to רבינא: What are these doubtful animals? If you say they are doubtful firstborns, the Torah said 'shall be holy,' meaning it becomes holy now, and not an animal that is already holy.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא מדפתי asks רבינא to identify the 'doubtful' animals the משנה treats as subject to מעשר. He rules out doubtful firstborns right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the tenth 'shall be holy' (יהיה קדש), which means it becomes holy through being designated as מעשר. A ספק בכור is already treated as holy because of the doubt, so מעשר cannot take hold on it. Some other kind of doubtful animal must be meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Doubtful cases: animals of uncertain status
Animals that may or may not be firstborns
'Shall be holy': it becomes holy now, through being designated
That is already holy
If you say: the opening of a suggestion the גמרא is about to reject

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha of Difti said to Ravina:
What are these doubtful animals?
If you say doubtful firstborns,
the Torah said 'shall be holy,'
and not one that is already holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא: מַאי סְפֵיקוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the reasoning about exemption to a clarifying question: what exactly does 'ספיקות' in the משנה refer to?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of doubtful animals the משנה is describing as subject to מעשר. The obvious suggestion, doubtful firstborns, is ruled out by the rule יהיה קדש, not already holy.

steps.title: The answer: lambs used to redeem doubtful firstborn donkeys
steps.stepSummary: The ספיקות are lambs used to redeem a ספק פטר חמור. As רב נחמן says, an owner with ten such donkeys separates ten lambs, tithes them, and keeps them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is the doubtful redemption of a firstborn donkey, in line with רב נחמן. רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: An Israelite who has ten donkeys in his house that may be firstborns separates ten lambs for them, tithes the lambs, and they are his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 'doubtful' animals are lambs separated to redeem donkeys that may be firstborns. It brings רב נחמן's ruling as support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פטר חמור is redeemed with a lamb, but when the donkey is only possibly a firstborn, the lamb's status is in doubt too. Since a כהן cannot prove any lamb belongs to him, the lambs stay with their owner. These lambs are ordinary, not holy, so they are subject to מעשר בהמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Redeeming a firstborn donkey, which is done with a lamb
Donkeys that may or may not be firstborns
Lambs or kids, the animals used to redeem the donkeys
He tithes them: separates every tenth as מעשר בהמה
And they belong to him: the owner keeps them

steps.whatToRemember: The 'doubtful' animals subject to מעשר are not doubtful firstborns, which are already holy. They are the lambs used to redeem a ספק פטר חמור, which stay fully with the owner, as רב נחמן rules.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב נחמן's ruling shows that when a כהן cannot prove his claim, the owner keeps the animals as his own, so much so that they are subject to his own מעשר.

phrases.english: Rather, the doubtful redemption of a firstborn donkey,
phrases.notes: He means the lamb that was separated to redeem a donkey that may be a firstborn.

phrases.english: and in line with Rav Nachman.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: For Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabbah bar Avuh:
An Israelite who has ten
donkeys in his house that may be firstborns
separates ten lambs for them,
and tithes them, and they are his.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא סְפֵק פִּדְיוֹן פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר, וְכִדְרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא מדפתי's question by identifying a different kind of doubtful animal.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ספיקות are lambs used to redeem a ספק פטר חמור. Per רב נחמן, the owner keeps them and tithes them.

steps.title: What was decided about the bathhouse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the earlier case of the disputed bathhouse and asks what the final ruling was.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was concluded about the bathhouse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the bathhouse case it raised earlier and asks for the final ruling. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא discussed a bathhouse that two people were fighting over, where one of them made it הקדש. It left open whether that הקדש takes effect. Now it asks for the resolution.

keyTerms.meaning: Bathhouse
What was concluded about it? A request for the final ruling

phrases.english: What was concluded about the bathhouse?
phrases.notes: This is the bathhouse two people were fighting over, which one of them made הקדש. The case came up a little earlier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of ספיקות and מעשר and returns to an earlier open question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the הקדש made by one of the people disputing the bathhouse takes effect.

steps.title: Resolved: property you cannot recover in court cannot be made holy
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבין reports that a similar case went from רב חסדא to רב הונא. It was resolved with רב נחמן's rule: property one cannot extract through judges cannot be made הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי חייא בר אבין said: There was a case at the house of רב חסדא, and רב חסדא brought it to the house of רב הונא. He resolved it from what רב נחמן said: Any property that a person cannot extract through judges, if he consecrated it, it is not holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real case that was decided and uses רב נחמן's rule to settle the bathhouse question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither person disputing the bathhouse could get it out of the other's hands through a court. רב נחמן's rule says a person cannot make הקדש something he could not recover through judges. So the הקדש made by one of them does not take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: An actual case or incident
He resolved it
To extract it through judges, meaning to get it back by going to court
He consecrated it: made it הקדש, Temple property

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's rule: if you cannot get property back through a court, you cannot make it הקדש. So in the disputed bathhouse, one person's הקדש is not valid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule ties the power to make something holy to legal control over it. You can only consecrate what you could actually claim in court.

phrases.english: Come and hear,
for Rabbi Chiyya bar Avin said:
There was a case at the house of Rav Chisda,
and Rav Chisda brought it to the house of Rav Huna,
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves out the verb; it means רב חסדא took the case to רב הונא.

phrases.english: and he resolved it from what Rav Nachman said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָמוֹן שֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לְהוֹצִיאוֹ בְּדַיָּינִין,
phrases.english: Any property that one cannot extract through judges,
if he consecrated it, it is not holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the bathhouse question from the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Following רב נחמן, property one cannot recover in court cannot be made הקדש, so the bathhouse הקדש is not valid.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Consecrating disputed property that one could not win in court does not take effect.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי יוחנן's rule about stolen items
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן's rule implies that property one can win in court can be made הקדש even before it is recovered. But רבי יוחנן says an owner cannot make a stolen item הקדש because it is not in his possession.
steps.simpleTranslation: So if he can get it back through judges and he made it holy, it is holy, even though he has not taken it back? But רבי יוחנן said: if someone stole an item and the owner did not give up hope, neither of them can make it holy. The thief can't because it isn't his, and the owner can't because it isn't in his possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the flip side of רב נחמן's rule and attacks it with a ruling of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said that what you cannot win in court cannot be made הקדש. That implies that what you can win in court can be made הקדש, even before you get it back. רבי יוחנן says the owner of a stolen item cannot make it הקדש because it is not in his hands, even though a court would give it back to him.

keyTerms.meaning: He made it holy, dedicating it to the Temple
To get it back through judges, meaning in court
Robbed
The owner gave up hope of getting it back
In his possession or control

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying the owner loses ownership. The item is still his. He just can't make it הקדש while it is out of his hands.

phrases.english: But if he can get it back through judges,
and he made it holy, it is holy,
even though he has not taken it back?
But didn't רבי יוחנן say:
If someone robbed and the owner did not give up hope,
neither of them can make it holy.
This one, because it is not his,
and that one, because it is not in his possession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what רב נחמן's rule from step 5 implies.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of רב נחמן's rule that recoverable property can be made הקדש before it is recovered
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן requires actual possession to make an item הקדש. Being able to win it in court is not enough.

steps.title: The bathhouse is land, which stays in the owner's possession
steps.stepSummary: The case is a bathhouse built into the ground. Land never truly leaves its owner's possession, so being able to win it in court is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think we are talking about a movable bath? We are talking about a bath fixed in the ground. Once he can get it back through judges, it is already in his possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining that the bathhouse was land, not a movable object.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן was talking about movable things, which a thief can carry off. Land cannot be carried away, so if a court would give it to you, it still counts as in your possession. That means both rulings are true, each in its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: A bath or bathhouse
Movable property
Land, or things fixed in the ground

steps.whatToRemember: Land that you can win in court is already counted as in your possession, so you can make it הקדש. A movable item has to actually be in your hands.

phrases.english: Do you think we are dealing with a movable bath?
We are dealing with a bath fixed in the ground,
where, once he can get it back through judges,
it already stands in his possession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (land versus movable items)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bathhouse was assumed to be movable, which would make רב נחמן clash with רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bathhouse is land. Land you can win in court counts as in your possession, so it can be made הקדש.

steps.title: A ברייתא on dividing a garment two people are holding
steps.stepSummary: רב תחליפא teaches a ברייתא: when two people hold a garment, each keeps what is in his hand and they split the rest equally.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב תחליפא from ארץ ישראל taught in front of רבי אבהו: two people are holding a garment. This one takes up to where his hand reaches, that one takes up to where his hand reaches, and they split the rest equally.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It brings a ברייתא about two people who are both holding a garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The part each person is actually holding counts as his. Only the middle part, which neither one holds, is split equally.

keyTerms.meaning: The West, meaning ארץ ישראל
Grasping or holding tightly
A garment or cloak

phrases.english: רב תחליפא from the West taught
phrases.notes: "The West" means ארץ ישראל, which is west of בבל.

phrases.english: in front of רבי אבהו:
Two people are holding a garment.

phrases.aramaic: זֶה נוֹטֵל עַד מָקוֹם שֶׁיָּדוֹ מַגַּעַת,
phrases.english: This one takes up to where his hand reaches,

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה נוֹטֵל עַד מָקוֹם שֶׁיָּדוֹ מַגַּעַת,
phrases.english: and that one takes up to where his hand reaches,
and they split the rest equally.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the garment from our משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each holder keeps the part in his hand, and they split the rest equally.

steps.title: רבי אבהו adds that an oath is needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו signals with his hand that the ruling only applies if they take an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו gestured to him: and with an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו adds a condition to the ברייתא without words, using a hand signal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holding part of the garment is not enough by itself. Each person must also swear to his claim before he takes his share.

keyTerms.meaning: Gestures or signals
An oath

phrases.english: רבי אבהו gestured to him:
And with an oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to the ברייתא in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The division in the ברייתא requires an oath.

steps.title: How does our משנה fit with the ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה simply says the two split the garment and does not mention each keeping what is in his hand. So what case is the משנה talking about?
steps.simpleTranslation: But our משנה teaches that they split it between them, and does not teach that each takes up to where his hand reaches. How can you find a case for it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the משנה can be explained if the ברייתא is right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people holding a garment each keep the part in their hands, the משנה should have said so. Since it only says they split the whole thing, it must be about a different kind of case. The גמרא asks what that case is.

keyTerms.meaning: They split it between them
How can you find such a case?

phrases.english: But our משנה,
which teaches that they split it between them,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא קָתָנֵי זֶה נוֹטֵל עַד מְקוֹם שֶׁיָּדוֹ מַגַּעַת,
phrases.english: and does not teach that this one takes up to where his hand reaches,
how can you find a case for it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the משנה fits with the ברייתא from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain reading of the משנה, that the two simply split the garment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the ברייתא, people holding a garment keep what is in their hands. The משנה's simple equal split needs a case where that rule does not apply.

steps.title: רב פפא: they are holding only the fringes
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that in the משנה both people are holding only the fringes, so neither holds any of the garment itself, and they split it all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: the משנה is about people holding the fringes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question by describing the exact case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each person holds only the fringes, neither has any part of the main garment in his hand. So there is nothing for either to keep by himself, and the whole garment is split.

keyTerms.meaning: They are holding
The fringes at the edge of a garment

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא is about people holding the garment itself, so each keeps what he holds. The משנה is about people holding only the fringes, so they split the whole garment.

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
It is where they are holding the fringes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to be about people holding the garment itself, which would clash with the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about people holding only the fringes, so the whole garment is split equally.

steps.title: Holding a 3x3 piece of the cloth counts as giving
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא learns from רב פפא that in a קנין סודר, once the receiver grasps a 3x3 piece of the cloth, it counts as 'giving,' because that piece is treated as if it were cut off.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: Learn from this. With a cloth used for acquiring, once the person grasps a piece three by three in size, we call it 'and gave it to his neighbor.' That piece is treated as if it were cut off, so the acquisition works.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא draws a practical rule from רב פפא's answer. Holding a 3x3 piece of the cloth is enough for a קנין סודר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא said that holding only the fringes does not count as holding the garment. That suggests that holding a real piece of the cloth itself does count, as if that piece were your own. So in a קנין סודר, the whole cloth does not need to change hands. A 3x3 piece in the receiver's hand is treated like a separate cloth that was handed over.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (a conclusion drawn from what was just said)
A cloth or kerchief, used for acquiring things (קִנְיַן סוּדָר)
Three by three (finger-widths), the smallest size of cloth that counts
It is as if it were cut off

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical size for a קנין סודר: the receiver does not need the whole cloth, only a 3x3 piece of it.

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya said: Learn from this:
This cloth (used for acquiring),

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּתָפֵיס בֵּיהּ שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ,
phrases.english: once he grasps three by three of it,
phrases.notes: Three by three finger-widths, the smallest piece of cloth that matters.

phrases.english: we apply to it "and gave it to his neighbor."
Because it is as if it were cut off, and so he acquires.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a new practical rule about קנין סודר from רב פפא's explanation of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a קנין סודר, grasping a 3x3 piece of the cloth counts as 'giving,' because that piece is treated as if it were cut off.

steps.title: Challenge from רב חסדא's case of a גט tied with a string
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why this differs from רב חסדא, who rules that a גט is not valid if the husband can still pull it back by a string he holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from רב חסדא? רב חסדא said: If the גט is in her hand and a string tied to it is in his hand, then if he can pull it away and bring it to himself, she is not divorced. If he cannot, she is divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב משרשיא's rule with a case that seems to point the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא says that if the husband still has real control over part of the גט, it does not count as given to her. The same should apply to the cloth: if the giver still holds most of it, the receiver should not be considered to have been given it. So why does holding just part of the cloth count?

keyTerms.meaning: And how is it different? (a formula for pointing out a contradiction)
A bill of divorce
A string or cord
Divorced

phrases.english: But how is this different from the ruling of Rav Chisda?
For Rav Chisda said:
If the bill of divorce is in her hand and a string is in his hand,
phrases.notes: The string is tied to the גט, so the husband is still holding on to it.

phrases.english: if he can pull it away and bring it to himself,
she is not divorced;
and if not, she is divorced!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב משרשיא's rule by comparing it to רב חסדא's ruling about a גט.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב משרשיא's rule that holding part of the cloth counts as giving.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא shows that if the giver still controls part of the item, it does not count as given. So the cloth, which the giver still mostly holds, should not count as given either.

steps.title: A גט needs a full cutting off; a קנין needs only giving
steps.stepSummary: A גט needs כריתות, a complete separation, which is missing while the husband holds the string. A קנין needs only נתינה, giving, which is present.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, with a גט, we need a 'cutting off,' and there is none. Here, with the cloth, we need 'giving,' and there is giving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two cases need different things, so they do not contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה calls a גט a 'ספר כריתות,' a document of cutting off. While the husband still has a hold on the גט, the cutting off is not complete. A קנין סודר only needs an act of giving, and handing over a 3x3 piece is a real act of giving, even if the giver still holds the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: Cutting off: the complete separation a גט must create
Giving: what a קנין סודר needs
There / here (used to contrast two cases)

steps.whatToRemember: Holding a 3x3 piece of the cloth is enough for a קנין סודר, because a קנין only needs giving. A גט is different, because it needs a full cutting off, so the husband cannot keep any hold on it.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the two cases disagree about what counts as 'in your hand.' They differ because a גט needs complete separation, while a קנין only needs giving.

phrases.english: There, we need a 'cutting off,' and there is none.
Here, we need 'giving,' and there is giving.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רב חסדא by showing the two cases need different things.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases: each one has a different requirement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case of the גט and the case of the cloth follow the same rule about holding part of an item.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גט needs complete separation (כריתות), so any hold by the husband blocks it. A קנין needs only giving (נתינה), which a 3x3 piece provides.

steps.title: רבא: A gold-trimmed garment is also split
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that when the grabbed garment has gold work on it, the two holders still divide it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If the garment had gold on it, they divide it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a new detail to our משנה's case of two people holding one garment. Even if it is decorated with gold, they split it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think the valuable gold changes the rule. רבא says the same splitting rule applies.

keyTerms.meaning: a garment decorated with gold thread
they divide it

phrases.english: Rava said:
If the garment was trimmed with gold, they divide it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the קנין discussion back to the garment case of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gold-decorated garment is also divided between the two holders.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא needed to say this at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא: why would gold make any difference? This sets up an answer explaining what new point רבא is teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ruling has to teach something new. If a gold garment obviously follows the same rule, רבא's statement seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: it is obvious

phrases.english: Isn't it obvious?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling as saying nothing new.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling about the gold garment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Gold is just part of the garment, so of course it is divided like the rest. Why say it?

steps.title: The case is when the gold is in the middle
steps.stepSummary: רבא is talking about gold that sits in the middle of the garment, in neither person's hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for when the gold is in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא means a case where the gold is in the middle, not in either person's grip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is narrowed so the ruling has something to say. The gold belongs to the shared middle part, so it is split.

keyTerms.meaning: it is only needed for a specific case
the gold
in the middle

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where the gold stands in the middle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's ruling seemed to teach nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is about gold located in the middle, between the two holders.

steps.title: That is also obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: even gold in the middle should obviously be split.
steps.simpleTranslation: This too is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again. If the gold is in the middle, of course it is divided like the rest of the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer still does not show anything new. Gold in the shared middle area is plainly shared, so the ruling still looks unneeded.

keyTerms.meaning: this too

phrases.english: This too is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first answer as still obvious.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the gold is in the middle
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Anything in the middle is split anyway, so the gold being there adds nothing new.

steps.title: Gold closer to one side is still shared equally
steps.stepSummary: The case is when the gold is closer to one person. He cannot force a cut that leaves him most of the gold, because the other can demand a different cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for when the gold is closer to one of them. You might have thought he can say, 'Cut it this way.' רבא teaches that the other can answer him: 'Why cut it that way? Cut it this way.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a sharper case: the gold sits nearer to one person, though not in his hand. רבא teaches that the gold is still split equally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The nearer person might want to cut straight down the middle, which leaves most of the gold on his side. The other person can say, 'Who says we cut that way? Cut it the other direction,' so the gold is shared equally. That is the new point.

keyTerms.meaning: it is closer to one of them
you might have said
it teaches us
what makes you choose this?
divide, cut

steps.whatToRemember: A gold garment is split so that the gold itself is shared equally. Being nearer to the gold gives no advantage when it is not in your hand.

phrases.english: No, it is needed where the gold is closer to one of them.
You might have said
that he can say to the other: Divide it this way,
phrases.notes: He means cutting along the line that leaves most of the gold on his own side.

phrases.english: so it teaches us that the other can say to him:
What makes you divide it that way?
Divide it this way.
phrases.notes: For example, cutting the other direction, so the gold ends up shared equally.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new, sharper case that answers the second 'obvious' challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case with a מהו דתימא / קא משמע לן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The one closer to the gold could insist on a cut that gives him most of it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The other can demand a different cut, so the gold is divided equally.

steps.title: Lender and borrower both holding a loan document: רבי's view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: the lender says the שטר is his and he only dropped it; the borrower says he already paid. רבי says the שטר must be confirmed through its signatures.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Two people are grabbing a שטר. The lender says, 'It is mine. I dropped it and found it.' The borrower says, 'It was yours, but I paid you.' The שטר must be confirmed through its signatures. These are the words of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא, similar to our משנה, about a lender and a borrower both holding a loan document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lender says the loan is still unpaid, so he should collect. The borrower says he paid and got the שטר back. רבי says the court first checks that the witnesses' signatures are real before the lender can collect with it.

keyTerms.meaning: grasping, holding on to
a written loan document
lender / borrower
be confirmed through its signatures

steps.confusionAlert: Here the argument is over a debt, not over the paper itself. The lender wants to collect the loan, and the borrower says it was already paid.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Two people are grasping a loan document.
The lender says: It is mine,
and it fell from me and I found it,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹוֶה אָמַר: שֶׁלְּךָ הוּא, וּפְרַעְתִּיו לָךְ –
phrases.english: and the borrower says: It was yours, but I paid it to you.
The document must be confirmed through its signatures,
These are the words of רבי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a ברייתא about two people holding a loan document.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: the שטר must be confirmed through its signatures.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: They split
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees with רבי and rules that the lender and borrower divide.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: They divide.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second opinion on the same case: the two sides split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since both are holding the שטר and we cannot tell who is right, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל treats it like the משנה's garment case and splits it. The borrower pays half the debt.

keyTerms.meaning: they shall divide

steps.whyThisMatters: The disagreement between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל sets up the גמרא's next discussion of how this case fits with the splitting rule of our משנה.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
They divide.
phrases.notes: They split the money in the שטר, so the borrower pays half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing opinion to רבי in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: the lender and borrower divide the debt.

steps.title: A note that fell into a judge's hands
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with a case where the disputed שטר fell to a judge. The תנא קמא says the judge never releases it, and רבי יוסי says the note keeps its presumed validity.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the note fell into a judge's hands, he should never take it out. רבי יוסי says: it stays in its presumed status.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from the last steps. It adds one more case: the disputed note ended up with a judge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the note is not held by the lender or by the borrower, so neither one has a grip on it. The first opinion says the judge keeps it and nobody collects with it until there is proof. רבי יוסי says the note keeps its normal valid status, so the parties act according to what it says.

keyTerms.meaning: A judge
He should never take it out (never release it)
In its presumed status (it is treated as valid)

phrases.english: If it fell into a judge's hand
phrases.notes: "It" is the disputed שטר from the ברייתא in the steps just before this one.

phrases.english: he shall never take it out.
Rabbi Yosei says:
it remains in its presumed status.
phrases.notes: He means the note is still treated as a valid note, so they go by what is written in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the same ברייתא begun in steps 20 and 21 by adding one more case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the note fell to a judge, the תנא קמא says it is never released, while רבי יוסי says it keeps its presumed validity.

steps.title: Does רבי let the lender collect everything?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי: if a confirmed note lets the lender collect the whole debt, that clashes with the משנה of שנים אוחזין, where two holders split.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: the note must be confirmed through its signers. And then the lender collects all of it? Doesn't רבי accept our משנה, "Two are holding a garment," where they split?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks back at רבי's ruling in the ברייתא and raises a problem with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי said the note must be confirmed through its signers. That sounds like once it is confirmed, the lender collects the full debt. But in our משנה, when two people both claim an item, they split it. So here too the lender and borrower should split the note, and the borrower should pay only half.

keyTerms.meaning: It must be confirmed through its signers (the witnesses' signatures are verified)
Collects (a debt)
Two are holding: the opening משנה of the פרק, where two holders split the item

phrases.english: The Master said:
The note must be confirmed through its signers.
And then the lender collects all of it?
But doesn't he accept our משנה?
"Two are holding" etc.!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks back at רבי's ruling in the ברייתא and attacks it using the opening משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's ruling that the note is confirmed and the lender collects
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both sides claim the note, just like two people holding a garment. The משנה says such claimants split, so the lender should collect only half, not all.

steps.title: Everyone agrees a confirmed note is split
steps.stepSummary: רבא in the name of רב נחמן explains that with a confirmed note, everyone agrees they split. רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל only argue about a note that is not confirmed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: when the note is confirmed, everyone agrees they split. Where they argue is when it is not confirmed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing what the argument in the ברייתא is about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי never meant that a confirmed note gives the lender everything. With a confirmed note, רבי also agrees they split, just like the משנה. The argument between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is only about a note whose signatures have not been confirmed.

keyTerms.meaning: Confirmed (its signatures were verified in court)
Everyone agrees
They divide (split it)
Where they argue

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רבי as saying "confirm it and the lender takes it all." With this answer, confirming the note only lets them split it. Without confirming, the lender gets nothing.

phrases.english: Rava said in the name of Rav Nachman:
With a confirmed note, everyone agrees they divide,
where they argue is about one that is not confirmed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23 by moving the argument to an unconfirmed note.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the argument is only about an unconfirmed note
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי lets the lender collect everything once the note is confirmed, which clashes with the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: With a confirmed note everyone, רבי included, says they split. The argument is only about an unconfirmed note.

steps.title: Why רבי requires the note to be confirmed
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds that even when the borrower admits he wrote the note, it must be confirmed. So if the lender confirms it they split, and if not, they do not split.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי holds: even if the borrower admits he wrote the note, it still must be confirmed. So if the lender confirms it, he splits. If he does not confirm it, he does not split.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רבי's side of the argument from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The borrower admits he wrote the note, but רבי holds that this admission alone does not let anyone collect with it. The court must still verify the signatures. If the lender verifies them, he gets half, like the משנה. If he cannot, he gets nothing. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל would say the admission is enough, so they split even without confirming.

keyTerms.meaning: One who admits that he wrote the note
It must be confirmed (verified in court)
He divides (takes half)

steps.whatToRemember: With a confirmed note, everyone agrees the lender and borrower split it, just like שנים אוחזין. For an unconfirmed note, רבי says the lender gets nothing, because even an admitted note must be confirmed. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says they split anyway.
steps.whyThisMatters: The question of whether a note the borrower admits to writing still needs confirmation (מודה בשטר שכתבו צריך לקיימו) is a well-known debate. This step ties that debate directly to our case.

phrases.english: Rabbi holds:
one who admits to a note that he wrote it,
it must still be confirmed.
So if he confirms it, he divides,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא מְקַיֵּים לֵיהּ לָא פָּלֵיג.
phrases.english: and if he does not confirm it, he does not divide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי's position in the answer given in step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the underlying principle that explains רבי's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It was unclear why רבי would give the lender nothing for an unconfirmed note when the borrower admits he wrote it.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי holds that an admitted note must still be confirmed. Confirmed means they split, and unconfirmed means the lender gets nothing.

steps.title: Why רבי says an unconfirmed note is worthless
steps.stepSummary: רבי's reason: an unconfirmed שטר is just a broken piece of pottery. Only the לוה's admission gives it value, and he says he already paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? It is just a shard. Who makes this paper into a real note? The borrower. And he is saying that he paid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי holds that the lender and borrower do not split when the note is not confirmed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unconfirmed note has no power of its own, so it only counts because the לוה admits he wrote it. But the same לוה who admits writing it also says he paid. Since his word is the only thing giving the note value, we accept his whole statement, including the payment.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
A shard of broken pottery, meaning something worthless
Makes it into, gives it the status of
The borrower
That he paid back the loan

steps.confusionAlert: רבי is not saying the borrower's admission does nothing. He is saying the admission comes as one package: 'I wrote it, and I paid it.' You cannot accept one half and throw away the other.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
It is merely a shard.

phrases.aramaic: מַאן קָא מְשַׁוֵּי לֵיהּ לְהַאי שְׁטָרָא –
phrases.english: Who makes this into a promissory note?
The borrower, and he is saying that he repaid!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבי's view stated in step 25, that an unconfirmed note is not split.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the reason behind a position
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the borrower's admission that he wrote the note makes it valid enough to split.
steps.terutzMaskana: The note only counts because of the borrower's word, and his word includes that he paid, so the note gives the lender no claim.

steps.title: Why רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says they split
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that a שטר the borrower admits writing does not need confirmation. So even without confirmation, they divide.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds: if the borrower admits he wrote a note, it does not need to be confirmed. So even though it is not confirmed, they split.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the other side: why רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the two sides split even with an unconfirmed note.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the borrower's admission makes the note fully valid, just like a confirmed one. Once it is valid, his claim 'I paid' does not take away its power. So it works like a confirmed note, which everyone agrees is split (step 24).

keyTerms.meaning: A borrower who admits that he wrote the note
To confirm the note in court through its witnesses' signatures
They divide it

steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument depends on one question: does a note the borrower admits writing still need confirmation? רבי says yes, so they do not split. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says no, so they split.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the dispute in a way that fits the משנה of שנים אוחזין, which answers the קשיא from step 23.

phrases.english: And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds:
One who admits about a note that he wrote it
it does not need to be confirmed,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא מְקַיֵּים לֵיהּ –
phrases.english: and even though he does not confirm it,
they divide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite view's reasoning, balancing רבי's reason from step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains what the dispute depends on
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once a confirmed note is split by everyone (step 24), it was unclear why רבן שמעון בן גמליאל would also split an unconfirmed note when the borrower claims he already paid.
steps.terutzMaskana: He holds that an admitted note counts as confirmed, so the split matches the rule for confirmed notes.

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא's case of a note that fell to a judge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the ברייתא: a שטר that fell into a דיין's hands is never taken out. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it fell into the hand of a judge, he should never take it out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It quotes the ברייתא's line about a note that reached a judge so it can explain what that line means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line was already mentioned in step 22, together with רבי יוסי's view. Now the גמרא brings it back on purpose to analyze it. The explanation of this case comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Fell into the hand of
A judge
Ever, forever

phrases.english: If it fell into the hand of a judge,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the disputed note from the ברייתא, the one the lender and borrower are arguing about.

phrases.english: he should never take it out,

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפַל לְיַד דַּיָּין לֹא יוֹצִיאוֹ עוֹלָמִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the explanation of רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the גמרא moves on to the next clause of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A disputed note that reaches a judge is never released from the judge's hands.
